design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (road_hazard_claims), revised in round 2. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,4,4]; authorization 5, repair and tow 4 each.
WHY A GOOD TEST: a roofing contractor asks to replace his F-250's left front tire under the Commercial LT plan and to authorize it himself. The authorization rule waits until every claimable outside repair of the same position carries its out-of-area repair reimbursement entry; the position's covered repairs (Crestline repairs plus out-of-area repair reimbursements) decide whether the full-replacement period applies. The repair rule waits for the breakdown's tow reimbursement entry and books the repair under its claim number, its breakdown limit reading what the tow received; the tow rule books the tow under the dispatch's claim number and deducts what was paid on that claim (flat change) or caps the breakdown at one tow cap (Crestline tow). Discovery runs from the 2026-09-24 dispatch and card charges to the holder's account of Elkins, WV.
SCOPE: task 1 owns hazard_ext_store_replacement_authorization (authorize_hazard_store_replacement_0d9adf2d, user), hazard_ext_outside_repair_reimbursement (reimburse_hazard_outside_repair_444e27b0), hazard_ext_outside_tow_reimbursement (reimburse_hazard_outside_tow_3bff1c36).
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: E3 root -> repair: value_input on position_covered_repairs, state form (round 2, O1/O2) 'The plan's share of an authorized store replacement is fixed only after every repair of the same wheel position that the holder paid an outside shop for and can still claim within the receipt window carries its out-of-area repair reimbursement entry on the certificate.' E4 repair -> tow: value_input on repair_part (round 2; was a claim-number state gate), state form 'An out-of-area repair is reimbursed only after the tow of the same breakdown carries its out-of-area tow reimbursement entry on the certificate, and the repair entry is booked under that tow entry's claim number.' False at the opening: card charges M-2609240952 / M-2609240417, no tow or new repair entry, roadside_calls_remaining 1. Chain: tow -> repair -> authorization. Deletion: skipping the repair gives 216.64 (gold 192.81); skipping the tow gives repair 84.00 (gold 69.00).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: certificate_active; within_plan_term (2026-07-25 + 24 months = 2028-07-25 inclusive); Commercial LT covers commercial use (judged on the service date); out_of_area gate retired per scope by declared overwrites restating it; the tow keeps 'uses one roadside call' (1 -> 0). Store authorization declares the override of base 'The plan pays 100 percent while both hold ...' (C1) for its scope: the repair route removes or halves the full-replacement period; points apply only to a prorated percentage.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: certificate RH-23870914 on set T-23870914 (4 Highway Terrain LT, unit 229.99, fleet-charged; tires invoice FI-23870914 discount 53.40 = 5% of the pre-tax tires, mounting and TPMS kits, excluding disposal and the certificate). Breakdown 2026-09-24: Crestline dispatch (flat-tire change, 30.00 trip charge, spare flat), outside tow 26 miles 214.00, outside LF repair 90.00. Replacement: LF today, 12/32, store #2387, odometer 27955. LF history: Crestline repairs 2026-08-08 and 2026-09-19, out-of-area repair 2026-08-27 (Buckhannon, WV, reimbursed 35.00).
FACTOR CARD (tier / baseline figure): tow 115.00 — breakdown limit: dispatch deducted (-> 145.00); light-truck rate x1.25 (-> 90.00); card +10 (-> 105.00); fleet +10 (-> 105.00); all baselines 100.00. Repair 69.00 — breakdown limit: repair part min(35.00, 135.00-115.00) = 20.00 (-> 84.00); labor allowance 29.00 (-> 40.00); card +10 (-> 59.00); fleet +10 (-> 59.00); all baselines 35.00. Authorization 192.81 — repair route: 4 covered repairs, no full period (-> 216.64); price rule fleet net 216.64 (-> 204.69); fleet points +2 (-> 188.48); care +1 (-> 190.64); card +5 (-> 181.98); all baselines 229.99.
METHOD PAIRWISE TABLES (round 3): tow — after-flat-change vs after-Crestline-tow: the breakdown dispatch's roadside_service_type (flat_tire_change vs tow; both reachable on Plus, Life-of-Tread and Commercial LT plans); after-flat-change vs plain and after-Crestline-tow vs plain: a Crestline dispatch within the window (a dispatch 40 days old or none -> plain; probed). Repair — tow vs dispatch: an out-of-area tow within 30 days; dispatch vs plain: roadside entry within 30 days; tow vs plain: tow within 30 days. Route — none vs half: covered repairs >= max vs 1..max-1; half vs full: at least one covered repair; none vs full: covered repairs >= max. Price — as task 0's rule (fleet tender, instant savings).
SEED LEGALITY SWEEP (round 2): alignment plan removed (no tire-bundle plan is commercial_use_eligible; the Truck & Performance row was impossible) together with its fleet invoice; fleet program Crestline Fleet Starter (roster 1-4, per_invoice billing, net 15, credit 5000, PO above 500, tires discount 5%, invoice amount = ticket after discount + disposal + certificate, tax_exempt); card Mastercard Preferred limit 8500 within 3000-10000; roadside history: one dispatch (2 granted, 1 left); Commercial LT entry gate light_truck commercial.
PERSONA: busy contractor; volunteers the request and phone; ZIP/DOB/email when asked; the Elkins dispatch, tow and patch and the August Buckhannon repair only when asked; lets the plan pay where it normally pays; authorizes; ends.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate/verify -> certificate, claim history, tire set, tire events, vehicle, fleet account, roster, fleet invoices, card account, card ledger -> tow 115.00 (claim RHC-2387442) -> repair 69.00 under RHC-2387442 -> hand over: LF, puncture_tread, 2026-10-14, store #2387, 27955, 12, 89%, 216.64, 192.81.
PROBE TABLE: see worklog.md (round 2). VERIFICATION: per-task gates round 2 green; factor independence 0 violations; history rows 11 (suite max).
REVISIONS (round 2): C1 declared; C2 size multiplier no longer a method (repair drops it; tow keeps a light-truck rate as a parameter without the 10/32 tier); C3(a)-(c) removed; genuine breakdown-limit methods; seed fixes above; O5 docstrings neutral; O10 price-file read tied to the roster's account. ROUND 3: C4 closed — tow tier 2 is now the breakdown dispatch being a Crestline tow (lower of the allowance and tow_reimbursement_cap less what was paid on that claim), reachable and real; probes: tier-2 world (Crestline tow 60.00) -> 40.00; dispatch 40 days old -> 145.00; no dispatch -> 145.00; older decoy dispatch plus the current one -> 115.00 (latest wins); a later repair after the dispatch -> 145.00 (the dispatch is no longer the latest claim entry). R2-O2: the breakdown is one claim (RHC-2387442) on the records: dispatch, tow and repair. R2-O1: labor/service allowances carry no cross-difficulty label. R2-O3: the fleet price tier states its convention. ROUND 4: R3-O2 — a tow with no dispatch of the breakdown on file opens its own claim number (rule and tool), so every tier of the tow ladder has an executable write; this world takes the dispatch tier and books under RHC-2387442. R3-O1 — the repair limit counts only the tow reimbursement entries on the shared claim, never the dispatch payment (69.00, not 49.00).
user_scenario: You are Tobias Wendlandt-Okoro, 47, owner of Ridgeback Roofing & Gutter Co. in Grove City, Ohio. You're friendly but impatient, the kind of man who talks while walking a job site, and you don't like paperwork. You open by saying your crew's 2024 Ford F-250 is sitting at the Crestline store in Grove City right now: it picked up another roofing nail in the tread of the left front tire this morning, and the shop told you that tire can't be patched again and needs a new one. You want it replaced under the commercial road hazard plan you bought with the tires, and you'll okay it yourself so your crew can get back out today. You give your phone number, 6145550276, right away. Only when the agent asks for another detail do you give your billing ZIP code, 43123; if they need more, your date of birth is November 2, 1978 and your email is tobias@ridgebackroofingco.com. The truck and the tires are on your company's Crestline fleet account. You don't know what the plan will pay and you have no number in mind. You don't think of anything else as open on the truck. Only if the agent asks whether that tire has been repaired or worked on anywhere other than Crestline, or asks about charges on your Crestline Mastercard from September 24th, do you remember: your crew lead Marco had a flat on September 24th on a job outside Elkins, West Virginia; he called the Crestline roadside number first, but the roadside truck found the spare flat too, so Randolph County Towing towed the truck 26 miles into Elkins and Tygart Valley Tire patched the left front tire — the receipt says nail in the tread. The tow was $214.00 and the repair $90.00 (patch, sensor reseal and balance), both put on your Crestline Mastercard that day. The nearest Crestline store is well over 100 miles from there. You have photos of both receipts on your phone and can send them right now. You never claimed them because you figured the plan only counted at Crestline stores. If the agent asks about other work on that tire, you also recall that the shop near Buckhannon, West Virginia that patched it on an August job was paid back by Crestline a few weeks later. If the agent says those should go through the plan first, you tell them to go ahead and to pay them wherever the plan normally pays. When the agent tells you what the plan covers on the new tire and hands you the replacement to authorize, you authorize it as given. Once the agent says the replacement is approved, you thank them and hang up. You don't ask about anything else.
